_comment: Roots for scripts/check_reachability.py, and the baseline it ratchets.
MOST ROOTS ARE DERIVED, not listed here: a decorated function, a method overriding a base
defined outside boltrig/, module-level code, a dunder, and a getattr with a literal string.
This file is for the rest - a process entry point, a CLI, a handler a config names by
string - and it is the honest weak point of the whole check. An over-broad root set
silently re-admits the defect the check exists to catch, so every entry needs a reason
naming WHAT calls it and HOW.
THE ROOT SET IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY ON THIS FIRST RUN. 145 functions are unreachable and 71
of them have no caller at all, and that raw number is more useful than a number laundered
through a list of roots someone guessed at in an afternoon. Declaring a root is how the
count falls, and each declaration is a claim a reader can check. So is deleting the
function, which for a good share of these 71 is the right answer: `redact` in kernel/pii.py
and `apply_rls` in store/postgres.py have no caller anywhere in the package.
The 71 include every name the repaired unwired-claims gate reports and every name its
waiver file waives, which is the corroboration that the graph is measuring what it claims:
select_or_generate_workflow, sweep_run_scoped, execute_write, push, consume, accept_once,
build_cell_scope, dev_principal_resolver, select_locale and store_bearer_verifier are all
here, arrived at from the other direction.
